days.label: Exodus 40 to Leviticus 3
days.key: And when any one bringeth a meal-offering unto the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon.
days.s: After the burnt-offerings, the law turns to the offering of flour; Rashi, on 2:1, reads nefesh, soul, rendered ‘any one’, as the poor man who usually brings it, counted by God as though he offered his soul, and Ibn Ezra, on 2:1, as naming the soul because the meal-offering is a freewill gift and the soul too is called willing.
days.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Ibn Ezra (Hebrew, On Your Way), on Leviticus 2:1, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 4 to 5
days.key: if the anointed priest shall sin so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he hath sinned, a young bullock without blemish unto the LORD for a sin-offering.
days.s: The law of the sin-offering for errors opens with the anointed priest; Rashi, on 4:3, reads his sin as the people’s guilt because they depend on him to atone and pray for them, and Sforno, on 4:3, as an error that befalls him only through the people’s own guilt, not from his heart.
days.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Sforno (Hebrew, On Your Way), on Leviticus 4:3, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 6 to 8
days.key: If he offer it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes mingled with oil, of fine flour soaked.
days.s: Setting out the peace-offerings, the law turns to the offering of thanks; the Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 9:7, reads it as lasting when all else ends: in the time to come every offering will cease but the thank-offering, and every prayer but thanksgiving.
days.src: The Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 9:7, the Torat Emet Hebrew text, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 9 to 11
days.key: Then Moses said unto Aaron: ‘This is it that the LORD spoke, saying: Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified.’ And Aaron held his peace.
days.s: When fire from the LORD consumes Nadab and Abihu after their strange fire, Moses speaks to their father; Rashi, on 10:3, hears it as Moses saying he had expected the sanctuary to be hallowed through himself or Aaron and now finds the sons greater than both, and Rashbam, on 10:3, as a charge not to mourn or leave the service.
days.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Rashbam (Hebrew, Daat edition), on Leviticus 10:3, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 12 to 13
days.key: All the days wherein the plague is in him he shall be unclean; he is unclean; he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his dwelling be.
days.s: The law of the skin plague turns to the one declared unclean; Rashi, on 13:46, with the rabbis, explains why he alone of the unclean dwells apart: having parted husband from wife and friend from friend by slander, he too is parted.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 13:46, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 14 to 15
days.key: And the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest go in to see the plague, that all that is in the house be not made unclean; and afterward the priest shall go in to see the house.
days.s: After the owner reports what looks like a plague, the priest acts before inspecting the house; Rashi, on 14:36, reads the order as the Torah sparing only earthen vessels, which no immersion cleanses, since other vessels can be immersed and food eaten while unclean.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 14:36, Hebrew text (Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 16 to 18
days.key: For on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins shall ye be clean before the LORD.
days.s: After the high priest’s rites, the chapter fixes a yearly day of rest and affliction; Sforno, on 16:30, reads the priest’s atonement as only lessening sin and readying it for pardon, while purity and full pardon come before the LORD alone, through confession and repentance.
days.src: Sforno, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 16:30, Hebrew (On Your Way), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 19 to 21
days.key: Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them: Ye shall be holy; for I the LORD your God am holy.
days.s: Heading a chapter of laws on worship, justice and neighbourly love, the LORD addresses the whole congregation through Moses; Rashi, on 19:2, reads the call to holiness as keeping apart from forbidden unions and from sin, and Ramban, on 19:2, as restraint even in what the Torah permits, lest one become a scoundrel within its licence.
days.src: Rashi and Ramban, on Leviticus 19:2, Hebrew in Sefaria’s export 3f10136 (2026): Rashi, Rosenbaum and Silbermann (1929 to 1934); Ramban, On Your Way New

days.label: Leviticus 22 to 23
days.key: And ye shall take you on the first day the fruit of goodly trees, branches of palm-trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and ye shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.
days.s: Closing the calendar of feasts, the law of tabernacles follows the harvest; the Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 30:12, reads the four kinds as Israel’s people, with both Torah and good deeds, with one, or with neither, bound in one bundle to atone for one another.
days.src: The Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 30:12, the Torat Emet Hebrew text in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 24 to 25
days.key: And if thy brother be waxen poor, and his means fail with thee; then thou shalt uphold him: as a stranger and a settler shall he live with thee.
days.s: After the laws of redeeming sold land, the chapter turns to an Israelite whose means fail; Rashi, on 25:35, reads the command as help before he falls, as one man can steady a load still on a donkey, while five cannot raise it once fallen.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 25:35, Hebrew text (Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Leviticus 26 to 27
days.key: And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid; and I will cause evil beasts to cease out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.
days.s: Among the blessings for keeping the statutes comes safety in the land; Ramban, on 26:6, takes the ‘evil beasts’ as ceasing to harm, since while the commandments are kept the land will be as the world before Adam’s sin, when no beast killed a man.
days.src: Ramban, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 26:6, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “On Your Way New”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 1 to 2
days.key: ‘The children of Israel shall pitch by their fathers’ houses; every man with his own standard, according to the ensigns; a good way off shall they pitch round about the tent of meeting.
days.s: After the census, the LORD sets each tribe’s place, three to a standard on each side of the Tabernacle; Rashi, on 2:2, reads ‘the ensigns’ as cloths coloured like each tribe’s breastplate stone, and Ibn Ezra, on 2:2, as figures, by the ancients’ account a man, lion, ox and eagle, like the cherubim Ezekiel saw.
days.src: Rashi and Ibn Ezra, on Numbers 2:2, Hebrew (Rashi: Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934; Ibn Ezra: “On Your Way”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 3 to 4
days.key: Now these are the generations of Aaron and Moses in the day that the LORD spoke with Moses in mount Sinai.
days.s: Turning from the census to Levi, the verses that follow name only Aaron’s sons; Rashi, on 3:1, reads them as Moses’ offspring too, since whoever teaches another’s son Torah is as if he begot him, and Ramban, on 3:1, by the plain sense, as Aaron’s priests, Moses’ line being the Amramites named below, keeping that teaching as a hint.
days.src: Rashi and Ramban, on Numbers 3:1, Hebrew (Rashi: Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934; Ramban: “On Your Way New”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 5 to 6
days.key: The LORD lift up His countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
days.s: The LORD gives Moses the blessing Aaron and his sons are to speak over Israel, and the verse is its closing line; Rashi, on 6:26, reads the lifted countenance as God suppressing His anger, and Rashbam, on 6:26, as God not hiding His face but turning to His beloved to be gracious.
days.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Rashbam (Hebrew, Daat), on Numbers 6:26, Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 7 to 8
days.key: ‘Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him: When thou lightest the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the candlestick.’
days.s: After the princes’ dedication gifts, the LORD gives Moses a charge for Aaron; Rashi, on 8:2, reads it as God consoling Aaron, grieved at having no part in that dedication, with the task of the lamps, and Ramban, on 8:2, takes that midrash as alluding to the Hanukkah lights of Aaron’s Hasmonean descendants, kept even after the Temple’s destruction.
days.src: Rashi and Ramban, on Numbers 8:2, Hebrew (Rashi: Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934; Ramban: “On Your Way New”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 9 to 11
days.key: And those men said unto him: ‘We are unclean by the dead body of a man; wherefore are we to be kept back, so as not to bring the offering of the LORD in its appointed season among the children of Israel?’
days.s: Unclean from a corpse at Passover, some men come before Moses and Aaron; Rashi, on 9:7, reads the law their plea wins as one fit to come through Moses like all the Torah, but said through them, since merit is brought about by the meritorious.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 9:7, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 12 to 14
days.key: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying: ‘Heal her now, O God, I beseech Thee.’
days.s: After Miriam is found leprous and Aaron pleads for her, Moses turns to God; Rashi, on Numbers 12:13, reads the prayer’s brevity as care lest Israel say that he stands praying at length while his sister is in distress.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 12:13, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 15 to 16
days.key: And they fell upon their faces, and said: ‘O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt Thou be wroth with all the congregation?’
days.s: When God bids Moses and Aaron stand apart that He may consume the assembly, they plead; Rashi, on Numbers 16:22, hears in the divine title One who knows every thought, and so who sinned, where an earthly king, not knowing the offender, punishes all.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 16:22, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 17 to 18
days.key: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
days.s: After the people blame Moses and Aaron for Korah’s dead, a plague begins and Aaron runs in with incense; Rashi, on Numbers 17:13, reads the incense as God’s answer to those who called it deadly poison: it stays plague, and sin is what kills.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 17:13, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 19 to 21
days.key: And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
days.s: On mount Hor Aaron’s garments pass to Eleazar and Aaron dies there; Rashi, on Numbers 20:29, reads the mourners as men and women alike, for Aaron pursued peace and brought love between quarrellers and between husband and wife.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 20:29, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 22 to 24
days.key: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, Thy dwellings, O Israel!
days.s: Brought to a third height to curse, Balaam sees Israel camped tribe by tribe and the spirit of God comes upon him; Rashi, on 24:5, reads the praise as drawn from tent doors set so that none faced another, and Sforno, on 24:5, as praise of the houses of study and of prayer, whose good reaches the whole nation.
days.src: Rashi and Sforno, on Numbers 24:5, Hebrew: Rashi’s of Rosenbaum and Silbermann (1929 to 1934), Sforno’s On Your Way text; Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 25 to 27
days.key: But among these there was not a man of them that were numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest, who numbered the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
days.s: Closing the census on the plains of Moab, the chapter sets it against the count at Sinai; Rashi, on 26:64, reads ‘not a man’ as the spies’ decree passing over the women, who held the land dear, and so the daughters of Zelophehad come next.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 26:64, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 28 to 30
days.key: Command the children of Israel, and say unto them: My food which is presented unto Me for offerings made by fire, of a sweet savour unto Me, shall ye observe to offer unto Me in its due season.
days.s: Opening a calendar of offerings for day, sabbath, new moon and feast, the LORD charges Moses; the Midrash, Numbers Rabbah 21:16, reads ‘My food’ as spoken by One who needs no offerings, the whole world being His and every beast offered His creation.
days.src: The Midrash, Numbers Rabbah 21:16, the Torat Emet Hebrew text in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 31 to 32
days.key: ‘Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites; afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people.’
days.s: God’s command opens a chapter where Israel kills Midian’s men and Moses orders every captive killed but the virgin girls; Rashi, on Numbers 31:2, reads the command as aimed at Midian, not Moab, which joined the scheme from fear, while Midian meddled in another’s quarrel.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 31:2, Hebrew (Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934), Sefaria export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 33 to 35
days.key: These are the stages of the children of Israel, by which they went forth out of the land of Egypt by their hosts under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
days.s: With Israel on the plains of Moab, the text names every stage from Egypt to the Jordan; Rashi, on 33:1, reads the list as God’s kindness, only twenty moves in thirty-eight years under the decree, and Sforno, on 33:1, as Israel’s merit in following Him through an unsown land, which made them worthy to enter Canaan.
days.src: Rashi and Sforno, on Numbers 33:1, Hebrew: Rashi’s of Rosenbaum and Silbermann (1929 to 1934), Sforno’s On Your Way text; Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Numbers 36 to Deuteronomy 2
days.key: THESE ARE the words which Moses spoke unto all Israel beyond the Jordan; in the wilderness, in the Arabah, over against Suph, between Paran and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Di-zahab.
days.s: With Numbers closed on the plains of Moab, Deuteronomy opens on Moses’ address to the people in the fortieth year; Rashi, on 1:1, reads the names as rebukes recalling where Israel provoked God, only hinted at for Israel’s honour, and Ibn Ezra, on 1:1, as places, absent from the earlier list of stages or named otherwise.
days.src: Rashi and Ibn Ezra, on Deuteronomy 1:1, Hebrew: Rashi’s of Rosenbaum and Silbermann (1929 to 1934), Ibn Ezra’s On Your Way text; Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Deuteronomy 3 to 4
days.key: But the LORD was wroth with me for your sakes, and hearkened not unto me; and the LORD said unto me: ‘Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto Me of this matter.
days.s: Moses recalls pleading to cross the Jordan into the good land; Rashi, on 3:26, reads ‘Let it suffice’ as ending the plea lest people call the master harsh and the disciple importunate, or as telling him much more is stored up for him.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Deuteronomy 3:26, Rosenbaum and Silbermann’s Hebrew text (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Deuteronomy 5 to 7
days.key: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
days.s: Moses follows the declaration that the LORD is one with this command, a chapter before ordering the land’s seven nations destroyed; Rashi, on Deuteronomy 6:5, reads it as love with both the heart’s inclinations, even at the cost of life, and with all one’s wealth.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Deuteronomy 6:5, Hebrew (Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934), Sefaria export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Deuteronomy 8 to 10
days.key: And thou shalt eat and be satisfied, and bless the LORD thy God for the good land which He hath given thee.
days.s: Promising a land of wheat, vines and olives, Moses turns to eating there; Ramban, on 8:10, reads it with the rabbis as a commandment to bless God whenever one eats one’s fill, for food and for the land, and so binding in every place.
days.src: Ramban, Commentary on the Torah, on Deuteronomy 8:10, Hebrew (On Your Way new), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Deuteronomy 11 to 13
days.key: Therefore shall ye lay up these My words in your heart and in your soul; and ye shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.
days.s: After warning that serving other gods ends in perishing from the land, Moses repeats his charge; Rashi, on 11:18, reads it as bidding Israel stay marked by the commandments in exile too, with tefillin and mezuzot, lest these be new on their return.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Deuteronomy 11:18, Rosenbaum and Silbermann’s Hebrew text (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)
